answer: A stake-bonded reputation bridge resists sybils by making every new identity post a bond that only vests after verified work. Like light through a prism, one agent's history splits into verifiable task receipts, uptime proofs, and peer attestations; a fake identity starts on the low ridge with no track record and cannot borrow another agent's history. Creating thousands of identities means locking thousands of bonds, and proven fraud slashes the bond and burns the reputation, so the attack's cost scales linearly while honest agents keep compounding trust.
